title: Leadership team survey results, read together: the team view
description: The team view shows a leadership group’s level and agreement on six themes. It is computed once at the close, for everyone at once.
kicker: Available now · free for one group
lead: When the scan closes, the whole group sees the same picture at the same moment. Each of six themes has a level and an agreement label. It shows where you agree and where views differ, and never one person’s answers.
summary: Level and agreement per theme, for the whole group at once.

items.title: Your view beside the group’s
points: See whether the group reads the team the way you do.

items.title: Early signs, without names
points: Shows where the leadership group is aligned, and where it is not.

blocks.title: Level and agreement, side by side
blocks.text: Each theme shows the group’s level on a scale of 1 to 5, and an agreement label: high, medium, or views differ. Both are computed once, when the scan closes.
points: “You agree on” lists the themes with high agreement.
“Your views differ most on” names where to talk first.
blocks.alt: The team view for a group of eight: six themes with a level and an agreement label each. Meetings is marked views differ.
blocks.caption: Eight of eight answered: views differ on meetings.

blocks.title: On the group’s Home
blocks.text: Once it opens, the team view sits on Home for every member, beside the scan’s count and a list of what needs them.
blocks.alt: The group’s Home: the closed scan with 8 of 8 answered, one focus area, and the team view’s six themes with their labels.
blocks.caption: Home after the scan has closed.

blocks.text: An average hides a split. A team that averages 3 may all agree on 3, or be divided between 1 and 5. The second needs a different conversation, so every theme carries an agreement label as well as a level. [How to assess a leadership team](/articles/how-to-assess-a-leadership-team) explains the research behind it.

blocks.text: Three ways a scan can end

items.title: Four or more answers
items.text: The team view opens for everyone at the same moment, computed once.

items.title: Fewer than four at the close
items.text: The scan gets one extension of seven days, for more answers.

items.title: Still fewer than four
items.text: No team view is made, and the answers are deleted.

blocks.title: Why four?
blocks.text: With fewer answers, one person’s view could be worked out from the result. The threshold is 4, it can be raised to 8, and it is never lowered. [Anonymity](/anonymity) sets out what the database enforces.

faq.q: When does the team view open?
faq.a: When everyone has answered, or when the scan closes after seven days, whichever comes first. Everyone sees it at the same moment.

faq.q: Does the leader see more than the members?
faq.a: No. The leader and the members see the same team view. No one sees anyone’s answers, a lowest or highest score, or a breakdown by person.

faq.q: Do late answers change the result?
faq.a: No. The result is computed once, at the close, and answers after it are not added. A new scan gives a new result.
That answers on a theme are spread widely across the group. It is a prompt to talk about why, not a verdict on the team.
